task: Draft a full patient preparation guide for a fictional outpatient contrast-imaging appointment at Riverstone Imaging. Organise the guide into three sections: Before Your Appointment, On the Day, and After Your Appointment. Use only the supplied facts. Do not add dietary restrictions, medication instructions, or safety guarantees not in the facts.

facts.text: The fictional radiology centre is called Riverstone Imaging.
Patients should arrive 30 minutes before their scheduled appointment time.
The booking confirmation includes a pre-appointment checklist that must be reviewed before attending.
Patients with known allergies to contrast agents must notify the centre at the time of scheduling, not on the day.
Patients must bring their referral letter, a government-issued photo ID, and their confirmation email to the appointment.
The imaging procedure itself takes approximately 30 minutes; total time at the centre including preparation and check-out is approximately 90 minutes.
A family member or friend must be available to drive the patient home; patients may not drive themselves home after the procedure.
Patients should rest at home for the remainder of the day following the appointment.
The referring clinician will contact the patient with results within 10 business days; patients should not contact Riverstone Imaging directly for results.
The centre's phone number for pre-appointment questions is listed in the confirmation email.

forbidden_additions: Dietary or fluid restrictions not in the facts.
Medication instructions or dosing before or after the scan.
A guarantee of contrast-agent safety or the absence of adverse effects.
preserve: The three required items to bring: referral letter, photo ID, and confirmation email.
The must-not-drive instruction and the requirement for a driver.
The 10-business-day result timeline and the instruction to contact the referring clinician, not the centre.
